questions.q: Friuli's native red takes the second half of its full name from the red stalks of its bunches. Name the grape.
questions.exp: Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso, the Court's Friulian red, is named for its red stem rather than for a red form of Refosco; it gives dark, plummy wine with high acidity, chiefly from the Colli Orientali and the Grave plain.

questions.q: Which of these DOCs on the Court's northeast list crosses from Trentino-Alto Adige into the Veneto, reaching the province of Verona?
questions.exp: Valdadige, Etschtaler in German, follows the Adige valley from the province of Bolzano through Trentino and south into the province of Verona, for whites, reds and rosés, many of them varietal. Alto Adige DOC and Trentino DOC stay within their own provinces, and Friuli Isonzo is one of the Court's Friulian DOCs, on river gravel near Gorizia.

questions.q: On a Soave Superiore DOCG label, what does the word Superiore promise beyond plain Soave DOC?
opts: Higher minimum alcohol and longer ageing
Grapes from the historic hill zone
questions.exp: Superiore is the general term the Court lists for a wine with higher minimum alcohol and longer minimum ageing than the basic denomination, and Soave Superiore DOCG is its example in the Veneto. The other three describe Classico, the historic heart of a zone; appassimento, as in Recioto; and the Charmat method of Prosecco.

questions.q: Cantina Terlano, one of the Court's two Alto Adige producers, is run on which model, shared by many of the province's best cellars?
questions.exp: Terlano, founded in 1893, is a growers' co-operative, and the Court notes that many Alto Adige producers are co-ops: a dozen or so of them take in most of the province's grapes from thousands of tiny holdings and make many of its finest wines.

questions.q: In which decade did Amarone della Valpolicella first reach the market as a wine sold under its own name?
questions.exp: Amarone is the dry wine of the dried grapes that once went only into the sweet Recioto della Valpolicella; houses such as Bertani began selling it under its own name in the 1950s, and it was raised to DOCG in 2010, the history the Court asks a candidate to know.

questions.q: Delle Venezie DOC, created in 2017 across Veneto, Friuli and Trentino, was set up chiefly to govern the varietal wine of which grape?
questions.exp: Delle Venezie DOC, with Trevenezie IGP beneath it, covers the whole of Veneto and Friuli and the Trentino half of Trentino-Alto Adige, as the Court says, and exists above all to control the great volume of Pinot Grigio grown on the plains.

questions.q: Which of these houses on the Court's list is known above all for Amarone della Valpolicella?
questions.exp: Masi stands with Bertani, Allegrini, Tommasi, Dal Forno and Quintarelli among the Court's Amarone producers; Mionetto and Bisol are on its Prosecco list, and Cantina Terlano is the Alto Adige co-operative.

questions.q: The Court ties orange wine to Friuli. How are the white grapes for such a wine handled in the cellar?
questions.exp: An orange wine is a white made like a red, the juice left to ferment on its skins for days, weeks or months, which gives amber colour, tannin and grip; Friulian growers in the Collio and at Oslavia revived the old method, often alongside natural winemaking.
